_comment: Greppable signals. Each rule names the upstream group/row it implements (Anthropic prompt-audit.md) or the lab source it comes from (labs.json ids). `labs` = which reader labs the rule is documented for; `contradicted_by` = labs whose official guidance recommends the opposite, which drops confidence to low for files those labs also read. Signals are candidates, not findings: the model running the skill classifies each one (keep list, provenance, trigger vs behavior text) before it reaches the report.

rules.why: Current Anthropic, OpenAI (Astra) and Google (Gemini 3) guidance all say plain direct instructions beat forceful ones; when many lines are critical the markers stop carrying information and over-apply.
Emphasis with no adjacent reason. Current models are highly responsive to the system prompt, so boosters written for under-triggering models now cause over-triggering and rigid gray-area behavior.

rules.pattern: 1a Pressure language - hedge on a requirement
rules.why: Hedges attached to real requirements are read literally as permission to under-deliver.

rules.regex: \b(do not be lazy|don'?t be lazy|be thorough|do not stop early|don'?t stop early|keep going until)\b
rules.why: Anthropic: current Claude models are proactive by default and this booster causes over-work. OpenAI says the opposite for Astra (it can stop early; define completion), so this is lab-dependent.

rules.regex: (think step[- ]by[- ]step|take a deep breath|<scratchpad>|<thinking>|think (harder|carefully before)|don'?t overthink)
rules.pattern: 1b Scaffold replaced by a feature - thinking prose
rules.why: Thinking depth is controlled by effort (Claude) / reasoning_effort (GPT) on always-thinking models; prose steering is redundant or ignored. Google still documents 'think very hard' as a lever on Gemini 3.

rules.regex: (show your (reasoning|thinking)|explain your reasoning before|write out your reasoning|["'`](reasoning|thinking|trace)["'`] (field|key|property))
rules.why: On Fable 5.x / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5.5 instructing reasoning reproduction, including a reasoning/thinking/trace field in JSON output or a tool input, may trigger a reasoning_extraction refusal; read summarized thinking, or ask for a short explanation of the answer instead.
Fixed cadences were written for models that padded or rambled; current models narrate appropriately and the harness can request updates.
Numeric output ceilings tuned against an older model's verbosity starve reasoning on hard problems; restate as audience/outcome. Keep if the cap is a hard format limit (a platform character limit).

rules.regex: (output only valid json|respond only with json|return only json|only output json)
rules.why: All three labs ship structured outputs / schema-constrained responses (and Claude Code has --json-schema); prose JSON forcing plus regex extraction is the dated stack.
Step scripts for judgment work over-constrain current models (Anthropic 1c; OpenAI: 'remove rigid recipes'). Keep where order is load-bearing (destructive or auth flows).

rules.regex: (it'?s usually best to|a good approach is to|you may want to consider)
rules.why: If removing the sentence would not change what is legal or how success is measured, it is strategy the model already owns.

rules.regex: (you will be graded|hidden tests?|you are being evaluated)
rules.why: Describes the scoring apparatus instead of the requirement.

rules.regex: (do not hallucinate|don'?t hallucinate|never make up|do not (infer|guess)\b)
rules.why: Anthropic: re-test whether still needed. Google: open-ended 'do not infer/guess' makes Gemini 3 over-index and skip basic synthesis; say what to ground on instead.

rules.pattern: 1d Fossil - retired model named in instructions
rules.why: A mitigation or claim tied to a retired model; nobody owns the removal, so prompts accumulate every generation's workarounds.

rules.regex: (hold (all )?(findings|results|updates) (for|until)|don'?t narrate|do not narrate|no interim (updates|messages)|no progress updates|don'?t explain what you'?re doing)
rules.why: Written for chatty models. Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 / Sonnet 5.5 already under-narrate, and between-tool notes now arrive as thinking blocks, so suppressors make agents look silent.
Written against over-formatting models; Fable 5.1 already under-formats. Keep when the output surface cannot render formatting (then say that, it is the reason).

rules.regex: (only use tools when (strictly )?necessary|minimi[sz]e (the number of )?tool calls|avoid (using )?tools unless)
rules.why: Sonnet 5.5 follows this literally and already under-uses connected sources; say when to check them instead.
The text is a diff against a previous prompt version the model never saw; state the current rule only.
Fine as a one-line focus-setter; a finding only when it substitutes for audience, product and quality bar.

rules.pattern: 2 History narrative - dates / incident IDs in rule text
rules.why: A rule's authority is the behavior it prescribes, not the incident that motivated it; dated archaeology rots and costs tokens on every load.
OpenAI (Sep 2026): requiring docs before every edit burns context; make pointers conditional ('read X for schema changes').
Astra runs tests unprompted; keep exact commands and required suites, drop the generic nag.

OpenAI: boundaries written to stop older over-eager models make Astra stop where continuing is fine; scope the gate to destructive, external, costly or credential actions. Safety rules are flag-only per the upstream method.

Descriptions ride in every request. OpenAI: the Codex initial skill list is capped (2% of context or 8,000 chars by default) and descriptions are shortened first, then skills dropped, so front-load the trigger; Anthropic: enumerated triggers generalize worse than intent categories.
OpenAI and Anthropic both recommend a small router SKILL.md with references loaded on demand.

Non-default sampling 400s on several current Claude models; GPT-6 models reject temperature/top_p when reasoning effort is not none; Gemini 4 and 3.6+ ignore custom values with a deprecation warning (400 in a future release). Keep only where a local or open-weights endpoint is the real target.

rules.pattern: 4 API fossil - manual thinking budget / disabled thinking
rules.why: On Opus 5.5 thinking is always on; thinking.disabled and budget_tokens return 400. Use effort.
Forced tool use returns 400 on Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Fable 5.1; use auto plus strict tools or structured outputs.
A refreshed time stamp can change the prefix each session. Confirm that the loader actually refreshes it.
Date-only metadata may change daily, or may be a fixed edit date. Confirm refresh behavior before changing it.
If expanded on load, a time placeholder changes the prompt prefix. A literal placeholder does not; confirm the adapter behavior.
A live run counter or remaining budget changes between requests. A fixed limit is useful context and should stay.
A fresh identifier can invalidate the prefix each session. Stable identifiers are not volatility; confirm how it is generated.
